cards.problem: Retried POST /orders calls create duplicate orders.
cards.decision: Deduplicate POST /orders by hashing the request body and dropping any repeat seen in the last ten minutes.
constraints: Dedup state lives in Redis with a ten minute TTL.
acceptance: Two identical POSTs within ten minutes create one order.
Identical POSTs eleven minutes apart create two orders.

evidence.summary: Retry storms in the September incident came from one mobile client version.

idempotent.definition: A request is idempotent when sending it again, from any client and with no special header, cannot create a second order.

retry storm.definition: Many clients resending the same request within seconds after a timeout.

cards.would_change_my_mind: Evidence that legitimate distinct orders often share an identical body within ten minutes.

teachbacks.problem: Clients that retry a failed POST /orders can end up creating the same order twice.
teachbacks.decision: Add an Idempotency-Key header to POST /orders and keep the first response for a day.
constraints: Keys belong to one client account.
A repeat gets back the exact stored response.
acceptance: Posting twice with one key inside a day makes a single order.
Reusing a key with a changed body is rejected with 422.
p99 latency grows by less than 5 ms under load.

evidence.summary: Last month's incident review found duplicate orders.

idempotent.definition: A request is idempotent when the same account resends it with the same Idempotency-Key and gets the stored first response rather than a new order; no key or a new key means a new request.

retry.definition: A client sending a request again, with the same key, after a timeout or server error.

teachbacks.would_change_my_mind: Proof that clients cannot keep a key alive across a crash.

examples: POST /orders twice with the same body: one order.
POST /orders with the same body from two clients: one order.
non_examples: POST /orders with different bodies: two orders.
DELETE then POST of the same order: two operations.
POST /orders twice a day apart with the same body: two orders.

termverdicts.note: Two orders from the same body is the bug I want to prevent, key or not.
